figures.heading: H/D contrast for quantitative composition
figures.viewer_title: Im et al., Matter (2021) — Graphical abstract: water-vapor uptake into an evaporating D₂O droplet
figures.alt: Original graphical abstract from Im et al., Matter (2021). A neutron beam passes through a sessile D₂O droplet. The schematic shows D₂O evaporation and H₂O vapor condensation. Below, neutron radiographs at 0, 300 and 600 seconds show increasing H₂O concentration, with the original transmittance grayscale and 0.5 mm scale bar.
figures.source_title: High-resolution neutron imaging reveals kinetics of water vapor uptake into a sessile water droplet
figures.source_label: Im et al., Matter 4, 2083–2096 (2021), graphical abstract
figures.modification: The complete original graphical abstract image object was extracted from the published PDF and losslessly encoded as WebP. Decoded RGB pixels match the source image; no cropping, resizing, redrawing, relabeling, contrast or color editing.
figures.caption: An evaporating D₂O droplet absorbs H₂O vapor from the air; neutron radiographs track the increasing H₂O content.

figures.heading: Published result · Water-vapor uptake in capillaries
figures.viewer_title: An et al., WCNR-12 proceedings (2026), Fig. 4 — D₂O capillary hydrogen profiles
figures.alt: Published neutron maps of hydrogen mole fraction versus time and distance in D2O-filled capillaries. Panel a, with the open end upward, shows a gradient near the open end. Panel b, with the open end downward, shows a more uniform profile. Color denotes H divided by H plus D from 0 to 0.2.
figures.caption: Open end upward (a): a hydrogen gradient develops. Open end downward (b): the profile remains more uniform. Color: H/(H+D).
figures.source_label: An et al., WCNR-12 proceedings (2026), Fig. 4
figures.modification: Cropped from the published PDF; data and labels unchanged.
figures.placement: Final block in Water vapor uptake in hygroscopic liquid, after the experiment explanation and related links.

figures.heading: PVA droplets · A rounder apex and fewer discrete bubbles
figures.viewer_title: An et al., arXiv:2606.01251v1, Fig. 1 — PVA and pure-water droplet comparison
figures.alt: Original optical and X-ray images compare frozen PVA solution in the top row and pure water in the bottom row. PVA droplets show a rounded apex and fewer discrete bubbles; pure water has a sharp tip and many bubbles. All six panels and scale bars are retained.
figures.caption: Optical and X-ray images compare frozen 3 wt% PVA solution (top) with pure water (bottom), using 10 µL droplets. PVA rounds the apex and reduces discrete bubble entrapment. Scale bars: white 1 mm; black 500 µm; red 100 µm.
figures.source_label: An et al., public preprint arXiv:2606.01251v1, Fig. 1
figures.modification: Original panels and scale bars preserved.

figures.heading: Tomography · Internal heterogeneity and surface texture
figures.viewer_title: An et al., arXiv:2606.01251v1, Fig. 2 — Frozen-droplet tomographic cross-sections
figures.alt: X-ray CT cross-sections of frozen pure water and PVA solution with original panels a through e and scale bars. Pure water contains discrete bubbles. The PVA specimen shows heterogeneous internal and near-surface features. CT contrast does not identify the local physical state.
figures.caption: CT compares discrete bubbles in pure ice with heterogeneous internal and near-surface features in frozen 3 wt% PVA droplets. Contrast alone does not establish local composition or physical state. Scale bars: black 500 µm; white 50 µm.
figures.source_label: An et al., public preprint arXiv:2606.01251v1, Fig. 2
figures.modification: Original panels and scale bars preserved.

figures.heading: Water droplets · Trapped bubbles and the final tip angle
figures.viewer_title: Im et al., arXiv:2511.20571v1, Fig. 2 — Trapped bubbles and tip angles
figures.alt: Original X-ray radiographs show water droplets frozen at minus 5, minus 10, and minus 20 degrees Celsius, with bubble-free vacuum comparisons. The graph plots measured tip angle against substrate temperature for ambient pressure and vacuum conditions. All panels a through f, scales, and graph labels are preserved.
figures.caption: X-ray images and tip-angle measurements of 1 µL water droplets compare substrate temperatures and ambient-pressure versus vacuum conditions, linking trapped bubbles to the final shape. All scale bars: 200 µm.
figures.source_label: Im et al., public preprint arXiv:2511.20571v1, Fig. 2
figures.modification: Original panels, scales, and measured data preserved.
